newsitem.title: USA: Three-time killer dies in Alabama electric chair.
newsitem.headline: Three-time killer dies in Alabama electric chair.

text.p: Billy Wayne Waldrop, a three-time killer who sought clemency after becoming a born-again Christian, died in Alabama's electric chair early on Friday for the 1982 murder of an elderly man.
Waldrop, 44, from Anniston, Ala., was pronounced dead shortly after midnight (0500 GMT) at Holman Prison near the city of Mobile, a prison official said.
The execution occurred a week after members of an evangelical prison group asked Governor Fob James to grant a reprieve.

Bill Gray, the governor's legal advisor, said more than a dozen Waldrop supporters put forward some persuasive arguments. Among other things, the group argued that Waldrop suffered a head injury before the murder that had altered his behaviour.
But state officials decided he had received a fair trial.

Waldrop was sentenced to death in March 1983 for the murder of Thurman Macon Donahoo, who was shot to death in his 100-year-old home in Alpine, Ala., on June 3, 1982. His appeal was later denied by the U.S. Supreme Court.

In an early confession that was later retracted, Waldrop told police that he and two accomplices killed the 72-year-old man and robbed him of a five-carat diamond ring, several guns, a tape player, silverware and $130 in cash.

The murder came months after Waldrop had been released on parole from a 17-month prison sentence for the fatal stabbings of two men in 1973. His initials had been carved into the bodies of the victims.
